question.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-5,-2],$ compute $P(X<-4).$
question.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a},\, & a\le x\le b, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-5,-2],$ so it has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3},\, & -5\le x\le -2, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<-4) & =P(-5\le X<-4) \\  & ={\int }_{-5}^{-4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-5}^{-4}\frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{-4-(-5)}{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
